correctness.rationale: For the precise character chi(2)=exp(2πi/10) in the real harmonic EITFF(11,11,3), the square-affine action partitions all 330 four-subsets into six size-55 orbits. Gram matrix for each representative is similar to a 12×12 cyclotomic matrix; the inspected certificate.py builds Q(zeta_55) entries and uses Faddeev–LeVerrier to check the complete degree-12 characteristic coefficients against the three polynomials in spectra.json, including exactly one simple zero for 12 columns in dimension 11. Positivity of the 11×11 sum of projections plus nonzero degree-one coefficient gives full span; exact quadratic-field Sturm checks isolate each least eigenvalue. Independent recomputation of orbit multiplicities and numerical eigenvalue roots gave class populations 165/110/55 and least roots ≈0.0389554/0.0849397/0.1859598. The numerical check is corroboration; the exact field and Sturm certificate algorithms were inspected for their mathematical soundness, not independently run.
residual_risks: Exact SymPy Q(zeta_55) computation was reviewed from source and table but not replayed in this run; independent finite numeric orbit computation cannot independently certify algebraic equality.
Claims apply only to the specified 11-plane character and 4-subsets, not all fusion frames.

value.rationale: The specific Fickus–Iverson–Jasper–Mixon real 11-plane EITFF is a natural nontrivial fusion frame. Exact erasure-reconstruction stability of all four-subspace selections and the complete orbit-stratified sharp lower bound are meaningful intrinsic geometric invariants not furnished by pairwise coherence alone, with precise extremizers. This is a motivated complete finite classification rather than an arbitrary small random computation.
residual_risks: No claim of general uniformly optimal erasure design across frames or other cardinalities.

limitations: The full exact 12×12 cyclotomic Faddeev–LeVerrier and Sturm verifier was inspected but not re-executed here; numerical roots alone cannot prove exact polynomial claims.
